project: Factory auth: five seams to A-
constraint: Apache-2.0 only. No imports from any ee/ directory. Reimplement, never port.

tasks.title: Scaffold mastracode/auth-kit package
tasks.detail: name @mastra/factory-auth, version 0.1.0, license Apache-2.0, type module, exports map with subpath exports per module (./contract, ./identity, ./capabilities, ./organizations, ./session, ./state, ./testing, ./conformance).
tasks.doneWhen: package.json validates; empty src/index.ts builds nothing yet.

tasks.title: Register the package in the workspace
tasks.detail: Root pnpm-workspace.yaml lists mastracode packages EXPLICITLY (mastracode/sdk, tui, factory, factory-ui, mastra-factory) - there is no mastracode/* glob. Add mastracode/auth-kit, then pnpm install at the root.
tasks.doneWhen: pnpm ls --filter ./mastracode/auth-kit resolves.

tasks.title: Toolchain config mirroring sibling packages
tasks.detail: Copy the shape from mastracode/factory. Strict TypeScript, colocated vitest, tsdown multi-entry matching the exports map.
tasks.doneWhen: pnpm --filter ./mastracode/auth-kit build && check && lint all pass on an empty package.

tasks.title: ESLint rule banning EE import paths
tasks.detail: no-restricted-imports with patterns: '@mastra/core/auth', '@mastra/core/auth/ee', '@internal/auth/ee', '**/ee/**'. Note @mastra/core/auth is banned WHOLESALE, not just /ee - its barrel reaches @internal/auth whose src/index.ts:373 does `export * from './ee'`, and packages/core/src/auth/ee/index.ts opens with a side-effecting `import './telemetry'`.
tasks.doneWhen: A file importing @mastra/core/auth fails lint with a message naming the reason.

tasks.title: CI module-graph test proving zero EE in the resolved graph
tasks.detail: Walk the kit's built output (or resolved import graph) and assert no specifier contains '/ee' and no module id resolves inside an ee/ directory. Lint catches source; this catches transitive resolution and survives a dependency bump.
tasks.doneWhen: Test passes on the empty package and is wired into the package's test script.

tasks.title: Negative-prove the boundary
tasks.detail: GATE. Temporarily add `import { buildCapabilities } from '@mastra/core/auth/ee'` to a kit module, confirm BOTH lint and the graph test go red, then revert. Record the procedure in the README so a future maintainer can re-verify.
tasks.doneWhen: Red observed and reverted; procedure documented.

tasks.title: contract.ts - the single import site
tasks.detail: Re-export the 8 interfaces (IMastraAuthProvider, ISSOProvider, ISessionProvider, IUserProvider, ICredentialsProvider, IOrganizationsProvider, IAuthHttpHandler, IAuthInit) and the 8 guards from '@mastra/core/server' ONLY. packages/core/src/server/auth.ts already re-exports exactly these by explicit name and is runtime-clean.
tasks.doneWhen: All 16 symbols re-exported and type-checked; no-ee test still green.

tasks.title: identity.ts - AuthIdentity type
tasks.detail: { id: string (required); email?, name?, avatarUrl?, organizationId? }. No vendor field - this is what replaces both FactoryAuthUser.workosId and EEUser.
tasks.doneWhen: Type exported and documented with the reason id is required.

tasks.title: identity.ts - toAuthIdentity normalizer
tasks.detail: Accepts flat { id }, { uid } (Firebase DecodedIdToken), { sub } (raw OIDC claims), and the { session, user } wrapper (better-auth, org on session.activeOrganizationId). Returns null only when no id can be found. Replaces mastracode/factory/src/auth.ts:190-231.
tasks.doneWhen: Unit tests cover all four shapes plus the null case.

tasks.title: identity.ts - IIdentityProvider escape hatch
tasks.detail: Optional capability `toIdentity(raw): AuthIdentity | null` plus a structural guard, so a provider whose token shape you cannot change can map itself. toAuthIdentity prefers it when present.
tasks.doneWhen: Guard + precedence tested.

tasks.title: state.ts - one OAuth state codec
tasks.detail: encodeState(returnTo) / decodeState(raw) with an explicit documented format, plus a parseStateId helper. Exists because the Factory passes the raw pipe-delimited value to handleCallback while packages/server splits it first - the disagreement that breaks auth/okta.
tasks.doneWhen: Round-trip tests including a returnTo containing a literal pipe.

tasks.title: session.ts - host-owned signed cookie
tasks.detail: HMAC-signed cookie over node:crypto with one declared name, correct SameSite/Secure derivation for same-site vs cross-site deploys, and mint/read/clear. Written fresh: the shipped CookieSessionProvider is Apache but only reachable through the EE-barrelled @mastra/core/auth.
tasks.doneWhen: Tamper test (modified payload rejected), expiry test, cross-site attribute test.

tasks.title: capabilities.ts - AuthDescriptor type
tasks.detail: { signIn: { kind: 'hosted' | 'credentials' | 'both' | 'none', label?, providerHint?, signUpEnabled?, credentialsBasePath? }, features: { logout, organizations, refresh, sessionRevocation } }. Deliberately smaller than the EE version: no RBAC, no FGA, no licence gate, no telemetry.
tasks.doneWhen: Type exported; scope boundary documented in the file header.

tasks.title: capabilities.ts - describeAuth() derivation
tasks.detail: Derive the descriptor purely from the Apache guards (isSSOProvider, isCredentialsProvider, isAuthHttpHandler, isOrganizationsProvider, isSessionProvider). CLEAN-ROOM: write this with ee/capabilities.ts closed. Different shape, different names, smaller scope.
tasks.doneWhen: Unit tests for all four signIn kinds against fake providers; a second engineer confirms it does not read as a paraphrase of the EE file.

tasks.title: organizations.ts - withSyntheticOrganizations
tasks.detail: Wrap any provider so it satisfies IOrganizationsProvider with a deterministic personal org. Must be a WRAPPER, not a CompositeAuth member: CompositeAuth implements only ISSOProvider/ISessionProvider/IUserProvider (provider/index.ts:169-171), so composing cannot supply orgs.
tasks.doneWhen: isOrganizationsProvider(wrapped) === true; ensureOrganization is deterministic across calls.

tasks.title: organizations.ts - resolveTenant host helper
tasks.detail: Generalizes the `user:${userId}` fallback that already exists at mastracode/factory/src/routes/provider-credentials.ts:74-75 so every org-scoped surface can degrade instead of 403ing.
tasks.doneWhen: Returns a stable orgId for a no-org identity; unit tested.

tasks.title: testing/ - composable fake providers
tasks.detail: fakeProvider() plus capability mixins (withSSO, withCredentials, withHttpHandler, withOrganizations, withSession, withInit) so a host test can build 'SSO but no orgs' in one line, with zero env stubbing.
tasks.doneWhen: Every mixin combination satisfies the matching guard.

tasks.title: conformance/ - describeAuthProvider suite
tasks.detail: A drop-in vitest suite a provider package runs in its own CI. Asserts the declared contract AND the four previously-undocumented obligations: a flat resolvable id, cookie-readable authenticateToken, agreement with the kit state codec, and an organization id (own or synthetic).
tasks.doneWhen: Green against a fully-capable fake; red against a deliberately broken fake for each obligation.

tasks.title: Kit unit test sweep
tasks.detail: Fill gaps so every exported symbol has direct coverage. The kit is the thing everything else trusts.
tasks.doneWhen: Coverage threshold set and met; no untested export.

tasks.title: Kit README and stability policy
tasks.detail: What the kit is, the EE boundary and how to re-verify it (from K6), semver policy for the contract, and how to run conformance.
tasks.doneWhen: README reviewed.

tasks.title: Packaging into mastracode/web's separate pnpm project
tasks.detail: web is a standalone pnpm project consuming monorepo packages via link:. Add '@mastra/factory-auth': 'link:../auth-kit', add --filter ./mastracode/auth-kit to the prebuild turbo filter list, and confirm scripts/monorepo-deps.mjs pin resolves it to a real version at build time (it requires a version field and a matching package name).
tasks.doneWhen: pnpm --dir mastracode/web run prebuild && build succeed; validate-output.mjs passes.

tasks.title: Add the kit to @mastra/factory and extend its lint
tasks.detail: Depend on @mastra/factory-auth workspace:*, and add the same no-restricted-imports EE ban so the Factory cannot regress the boundary either.
tasks.doneWhen: factory builds and lints with the kit as a dependency.

tasks.title: Compat flag for the identity change
tasks.detail: MASTRACODE_AUTH_IDENTITY_V2, defaulting OFF. The identity/session/logout changes all land together and are the only ones that can break a live sign-in; the flag keeps a one-command rollback for a release.
tasks.doneWhen: Flag reads once at module scope, both paths reachable in tests.

tasks.title: Route identity through the kit
tasks.detail: Replace toFactoryAuthUser (auth.ts:190-231) with the kit's toAuthIdentity behind the flag. This is the change that makes a { uid } or raw-JWT provider stop authenticating as nobody.
tasks.doneWhen: Both flag states pass the existing auth suite.

tasks.title: Drop workosId from the neutral user shapes
tasks.detail: FactoryAuthUser (auth.ts:41-43) and TestAuthUser (test-utils.ts:27-28). A vendor name in the neutral type is the tell that identity was never really abstracted.
tasks.doneWhen: grep for workosId in mastracode/ returns nothing outside changelogs.

tasks.title: Delete the WorkOS type-test helpers
tasks.detail: isWorkOSAuth (auth.ts:325) and getWorkOSProvider (auth.ts:334), plus their call sites. Verified dead on production paths - the audit's severity downgrade stands, but they are the last instanceof coupling in the neutral module.
tasks.doneWhen: No instanceof against a provider class anywhere in mastracode/factory/src.

tasks.title: Delete the WORKOS_* env fallback provider
tasks.detail: envFallbackAuthProvider (auth.ts:161-179) and the static MastraAuthWorkos import at auth.ts:1. mountFactoryAuth then requires an explicit provider. Update the two suites that relied on the implicit env path to pass a fake instead.
tasks.doneWhen: mountFactoryAuth has no env reads; suites pass without stubbing WORKOS_*.

tasks.title: Remove @mastra/auth-workos from the Factory
tasks.detail: Drop the dependency (package.json:58) and delete the vi.mock('@mastra/auth-workos') calls both gate suites are forced to carry.
tasks.doneWhen: A vendor auth package no longer appears in the neutral module's dependency graph.

tasks.title: Adopt the kit state codec on login and callback
tasks.detail: Replace encodeState/decodeState (auth.ts:434, :443) and fix the handoff at auth.ts:569 so what handleCallback receives matches what the contract documents.
tasks.doneWhen: A provider written against the documented codec completes a callback under BOTH hosts.

tasks.title: Session cookie minting and clearing via the kit
tasks.detail: Use the kit session module for the ISessionProvider fallback branch (auth.ts:576-593) and for clearing. Keep honoring provider-supplied cookies when handleCallback returns them - that path is what WorkOS and Okta already use.
tasks.doneWhen: Both cookie sources tested; the un-join regex at auth.ts:281-282 has a test pinning the malformed-header case it defends against.

tasks.title: Logout revokes, and moves to POST
tasks.detail: Call destroySession on the SSO path (auth.ts:603) where the provider implements it, and move logout to POST - a GET logout is CSRF-triggerable by any . Keep a GET shim that redirects for one release so bookmarked links do not break.
tasks.doneWhen: destroySession observed called; POST is the documented route; GET shim tested.

tasks.title: Session refresh parity with packages/server
tasks.detail: packages/server transparently refreshes (helpers.ts:397-417); the Factory does not, so a provider's refreshSession works on /api/* and silently does nothing on Factory routes. Close the third behavioural divergence.
tasks.doneWhen: A fake provider with an expiring session is transparently refreshed on a Factory route.

tasks.title: resolveTenant wired into the RouteAuth seam
tasks.detail: factoryAuthTenant returns a resolved tenant with a synthetic org when the provider has none, so the seven org-gated route groups stop 403ing an otherwise valid user.
tasks.doneWhen: A no-org fake provider reaches the board.

tasks.title: Remove the org-required throw in the workspace layer
tasks.detail: workspace.ts:316 throws when organizationId is absent. Route it through resolveTenant; keep the throw only for the genuinely identity-less server-side caller case the comment describes.
tasks.doneWhen: No-org user opens a session; identity-less caller still throws.

tasks.title: Migrate workspace.ts onto RouteAuth
tasks.detail: Stop importing the auth module directly (workspace.ts:13) and reading identity off the raw request context. One of three modules that bypass the port.
tasks.doneWhen: No direct auth-module import remains in workspace.ts.

tasks.title: Migrate rules/binding-context.ts onto RouteAuth
tasks.detail: Second bypass module (binding-context.ts:4).
tasks.doneWhen: No direct auth-module import remains.

tasks.title: Migrate github/session-subscriptions.ts onto RouteAuth
tasks.detail: Third bypass module (session-subscriptions.ts:5). After this, RouteAuth is the only identity path, not merely the preferred one.
tasks.doneWhen: grep confirms RouteAuth is the sole identity route into mastracode/factory/src.

tasks.title: Backend exit-gate tests
tasks.detail: GATE. (1) a cookie-only request authenticates through the gate - the browser path, uncovered today; (2) a { uid }-shaped provider authenticates end to end; (3) a no-org provider reaches the board without a 403; (4) each capability branch - SSO, http-handler, neither - drives real app.request() responses; (5) the { session, tokens } callback branch at auth.ts:576, unasserted in both hosts today.
tasks.doneWhen: All five pass with the flag ON.

tasks.title: Flip the compat flag on by default and soak
tasks.detail: Default V2 on. Hold one release with the legacy path still reachable by env override.
tasks.doneWhen: A release ships with V2 default and no rollback.

tasks.title: Delete the flag and the legacy sniffer
tasks.detail: Remove the flag, the old toFactoryAuthUser, and the dual-path tests. Deferred deliberately - this is the one task that should wait a release.
tasks.doneWhen: One identity path remains.

tasks.title: /auth/me emits the capability descriptor
tasks.detail: Replace the bare provider.name payload (auth.ts:400-424, :407) with describeAuth(provider). The handler already evaluates isCredentialsProvider one line earlier at :406 and throws the answer away. Keep name in the payload for one release so the SPA fallback still works.
tasks.doneWhen: Descriptor present in the response for every capability shape.

tasks.title: Server-side descriptor tests
tasks.detail: Assert the /auth/me payload for hosted, credentials, both and none, using the kit's fakes.
tasks.doneWhen: Four cases pinned.

tasks.title: SPA reads the descriptor
tasks.detail: Extend FactoryAuthState with the descriptor and parse it in fetchAuthState, tolerating its absence (older server) by falling back to the name.
tasks.doneWhen: Type and parse tested against both payload shapes.

tasks.title: SignInPage branches on capability
tasks.detail: Replace the two string comparisons at SignInPage.tsx:154-156 with descriptor.signIn.kind. Unknown providers get a correct generic hosted-login button instead of the GitHub logo and 'Continue with GitHub' at :157/:225. Keep the name check behind a clearly labelled legacy branch.
tasks.doneWhen: All four kinds render correctly, including an unrecognised provider.

tasks.title: Credentials endpoint comes from the descriptor
tasks.detail: services/auth.ts:74 posts to `${baseUrl}/auth/api/${path}` with callers passing 'sign-in/email' (:103) and 'sign-up/email' (:107) - better-auth's WIRE FORMAT, not just its name. Take the base path from descriptor.signIn.credentialsBasePath so any IAuthHttpHandler provider works untouched.
tasks.doneWhen: A fake http-handler provider on a different base path signs in.

tasks.title: Remaining provider-name reads in the SPA
tasks.detail: Sweep for any other provider-name branch. The Settings label already humanizes unknown names, so this is mostly confirmation.
tasks.doneWhen: No behavioural branch on a provider name outside the labelled legacy fallback.

tasks.title: MSW tests for every sign-in kind
tasks.detail: Follow the playground-msw-tests approach (primary for these packages): drive the real client + React Query stack through MSW handlers. Cover hosted, credentials, both, none, and an unknown provider name with a descriptor present.
tasks.doneWhen: pnpm --filter ./mastracode/factory-ui test:msw green.

tasks.title: CI test banning provider-name literals in the SPA
tasks.detail: GATE. Scan factory-ui/src for 'better-auth', 'mastra-studio', 'workos' etc. and fail on any hit outside the labelled legacy branch and its test fixtures. This is what stops the UI seam sliding back.
tasks.doneWhen: Test passes; adding a name literal makes it fail.

tasks.title: Remove the legacy name fallback
tasks.detail: After one release, drop the name branch in the SPA and the name field from /auth/me. Deferred with B19 for the same reason.
tasks.doneWhen: Descriptor is the only input to the sign-in decision.

tasks.title: Conformance baseline: better-auth
tasks.detail: Start with the richest provider (IAuthHttpHandler + IOrganizationsProvider + IAuthInit) to shake out suite bugs against something that should pass.
tasks.doneWhen: Green, or failures triaged as suite bugs and fixed.

tasks.title: Conformance baseline: workos and studio
tasks.detail: The two providers that run the Factory today. Any failure here is a suite bug or a real latent defect - both worth knowing.
tasks.doneWhen: Both green or defects filed.

tasks.title: Conformance on okta - expect red
tasks.detail: Should fail the state obligation immediately. This is the suite proving its worth: auth/okta has zero handleCallback coverage today, which is exactly why the defect shipped.
tasks.doneWhen: Suite reproduces the callback failure.

tasks.title: Fix the okta state contract
tasks.detail: getLoginUrl stores under the UUID half (auth-provider.ts:379-383) while handleCallback looks the value up verbatim (:412). Adopt the kit codec on both sides, and add the handleCallback tests that were missing.
tasks.doneWhen: C3 goes green; a full sign-in completes under the Factory.

tasks.title: Conformance on supabase and firebase - decide and act
tasks.detail: Both are two-method bearer validators today. Either adapt them (Supabase: ISSOProvider over signInWithOAuth; Firebase: IAuthHttpHandler over Identity Toolkit REST, since Admin SDK has no hosted-login URL) plus withSyntheticOrganizations, or mark them explicitly unsupported-with-reason. Both must also override authorizeUser, whose shipped implementations 403 core /api/* without bespoke infrastructure.
tasks.doneWhen: Each provider either passes conformance or carries a documented unsupported marker.

tasks.title: Retire the 60-second boot tests
tasks.detail: Provider-selection branches each cost a 60s module re-import under vi.stubEnv (index.test.ts:315). The factoryConfigs capture seam already exists in the same file (:6-16) and is already used at :81 - move the auth ladder assertions onto it.
tasks.doneWhen: The auth env-group describes run in seconds, asserting on captured config rather than a booted app.

tasks.title: Conformance wired into CI for every shipped provider
tasks.detail: GATE. Every provider you ship runs conformance in CI. A new provider that skips it should be impossible to merge.
tasks.doneWhen: CI fails when a shipped provider's conformance test is deleted.

tasks.title: Capability reference table
tasks.detail: Interface -> routes unlocked -> methods required, for all eight. Zero occurrences of these interface names exist in docs today. Follow docs/AGENTS.md and the styleguides.
tasks.doneWhen: Table published and matches the guards in contract.ts.

tasks.title: The four obligations, promoted to documented contract
tasks.detail: Flat resolvable id, cookie-first authenticateToken, the state codec, and the organization requirement - each with the consuming code named and the kit helper that satisfies it.
tasks.doneWhen: Every obligation the conformance suite asserts is documented.

tasks.title: Write-a-provider guide, end to end
tasks.detail: From empty package to working sign-in, ending with 'now run the conformance suite'. Use a generic OIDC provider as the worked example, since that is the shape Cognito and most enterprise SSO reduce to.
tasks.doneWhen: Complete draft reviewed.

tasks.title: CI type-checks every doc example
tasks.detail: Extract examples into compiled fixtures so the guide cannot silently rot against the contract it documents.
tasks.doneWhen: A deliberate breaking change to the contract makes the docs job fail.

tasks.title: Validate the guide on a real reader
tasks.detail: GATE. Someone who has not worked on this writes a working provider from the guide alone, with no help. That is the actual A- test for documentation; everything before it is a proxy.
tasks.doneWhen: They succeed, or the guide is revised until they do.

tasks.title: Update the mastracode READMEs
tasks.detail: The new provider ladder and local setup. Also the gotcha that with any auth provider active, env model keys are ignored (TenantCredentialStore.allowEnvironmentFallback = false) - keys go in through the UI. That currently reads as a bug.
tasks.doneWhen: A fresh clone can run locally from the README alone.

tasks.title: Changesets
tasks.detail: Per .mastracode/commands/changeset.md: one changeset per logical group, not one giant multi-package file. Likely groups: the kit (new package, minor), @mastra/factory (minor - behaviour change), auth/okta (patch - callback fix), factory-ui (patch).
tasks.doneWhen: Changesets written and reviewed for audience fit.

tasks.title: Re-grade against the five exit-criteria sets
tasks.detail: Walk the A- criteria for contract, backend, UI, testability and docs. Anything short gets a follow-up task, not a rounded-up grade.
tasks.doneWhen: All five criteria sets demonstrably met, or gaps explicitly accepted in writing.

tasks.title: Deferred cleanup release
tasks.detail: The one-release-later tasks: flag removal and legacy fallback deletion. Tracked here so they are not forgotten.
tasks.doneWhen: Both deferred deletions shipped.

notes: B18, B19, U9 and R3 are deliberately deferred by one release; they are not on the path to A-.
Two engineers parallelize cleanly after K7: one takes the K8-K10/K15-K18 identity+conformance spine, the other takes K11-K14 (state, session, capabilities). They rejoin at K17.
Lane U cannot start before U1, which needs K14. Lane C cannot start before K18. Lane D trails both.
